title: Neoadjuvant 2X-121 Plus Standard-of-Care Chemotherapy in Patients With Oligometastatic Colorectal Cancer to the Liver Undergoing Curative-Intent Surgery
official: A Phase 2 Study of Neoadjuvant 2X-121 Plus Standard-of-Care Chemotherapy in Patients With Oligometastatic Colorectal Cancer to the Liver Undergoing Curative-Intent Surgery
summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and activity of 2X-121 with standard-of-care chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant setting for patients with colorectal cancer with liver metastases undergoing curative intent oligometastatic liver resection. The co-primary endpoints are change in tumor cell CD44 expression and change in tumor cell beta-catenin levels in colorectal liver metastases following treatment with 2X-121 and to assess safety and toxicities. Secondary endpoints include 1-year event-free survival and ctDNA negativity for 6 months postoperatively.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* ECOG (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group) performance status of 0-2.
* Have histologically proven metastatic (Stage IV) mismatch repair proficient (pMMR) or microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer.
* Cohort A only: Have received for 3 month of fluoropyrimidine based chemotherapy \[fluoropyrimidine (5-FU or capecitabine) with either oxaliplatin and/or irinotecan\] prior to curative intent surgical resection. The addition of a VEGF or EGFR inhibitor (bevacizumab, cetuximab, panitumumab) to one of these regimens is also permitted.
* Cohort B only: Planned for, but not yet started, 3 to 4 months of fluoropyrimidine based chemotherapy \[fluoropyrimidine (5-FU or capecitabine) with either oxaliplatin and/or irinotecan\] prior to curative intent surgical resection. The addition of a VEGF or EGFR inhibitor (bevacizumab, cetuximab, panitumumab) to one of these regimens is also permitted.
* Must have three or less hepatic lesions as the solitary site of radiographically visible distant metastatic disease with plans for curative intent surgical resection.
* Patient acceptance to tumor biopsy of metastatic liver lesion prior to treatment if lesion can be biopsied with acceptable clinical risk (as judged by the investigator).
* Patients must have adequate organ and marrow function defined by study-specified laboratory tests.
* LVEF assessment with documented LVEF ≥ 45% by either TTE or MUGA (TTE preferred) within 6 months from first study drug administration.
* Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test.
* For both Women and Men, must use acceptable form of birth control while on study.
* Ability to understand and willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient has received an investigational agent or used an investigational device within 28 days of the first dose of study drug.
* Patient is expected to require any other form of systemic or localized antineoplastic therapy while on study.
* Patient with a history of palliative radiation received within 2 weeks of anticipated cycle 1 day 1 of investigational agent.
* Has a known additional malignancy that is progressing and has required active treatment within the past 1 year.
* Is taking a strong cytochrome P450 inhibitor.
* Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, uncontrolled infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina, cardiac arrhythmia, metastatic cancer, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements.
* Patient is, at the time of signing informed consent, a regular user (including "recreational use") of any illicit drugs or other substance abuse (including alcohol) that could potentially interfere with adherence to study procedures or requirements.
* Subjects unable to undergo venipuncture and/or tolerate venous access.
* Pregnant or breastfeeding.
* Patient is unwilling or unable to follow the study schedule for any reason.
* Patient received a live vaccine within 30 days of planned start of study medication.
* Uncontrolled intercurrent active medical and/or psychiatric illness/social psychosocial problems that that would limit compliance with study requirements.
sponsor: Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center at Johns Hopkins
